title: Investing, gambling or scam?
blurb: How to tell real investing from gambling and scams, and the red flags that give scams away.
t1.title: Three buckets
t1.hook: Four offers land on Asha's phone. One is a betting app. One is a long-term basket with no guarantee. One promises "guaranteed 30% a month". One is a hyped coin. Your mission: sort them.
t1.define: **Investing** means owning or lending something with real value, and the returns are uncertain. **Gambling** is mostly chance, with no real value behind it. A **scam** lies about the returns or about how it works.
t1.note: Some offers are hard to sort. Look at what is really behind the money, and whether the seller is honest about the risk.
q1.prompt: A betting app lets you win or lose money on the result of a match. Which bucket is it?
q1.hint: Is the outcome mostly chance, with nothing of real value behind it?
q1.explain: The outcome is decided mostly by chance and nothing of value stands behind it. That is gambling.
q2.prompt: A long-term basket of many companies, with no guarantee, and an honest warning that it can fall. Which bucket is it?
q2.hint: It owns real companies, and the seller is honest about the risk.
q2.explain: It owns real things, makes no false promise, and warns about risk. That is investing.
q3.prompt: A scheme promises "guaranteed 30% a month, zero risk". Which bucket is it?
q3.hint: Can anyone honestly promise a return like that?
q3.explain: A guaranteed, huge return with no risk is a lie. That is a scam.
t2.title: Promised returns
t2.define: A fixed, high return with no risk is the biggest warning sign. Real investments cannot promise returns, because nobody controls what prices will do.
t2.tradeoff: The higher the promise, the more likely it is false. High returns come with high risk, never with a guarantee.
q4.prompt: A scheme promises {monthly} every month. Without compounding, how much is that in a year? Type a percentage.
q4.hint: Multiply the monthly rate by the number of months.
q4.explain: {monthly} a month for {months} months is {yearly} a year. Almost nothing real pays that.
q5.prompt: Why can no one honestly guarantee a high return?
q5.opt.a: Returns depend on things nobody controls
q5.opt.b: The seller sets the returns, so they can promise what they like
q5.fb.b: The seller does not control what prices do. Anyone who promises a high return is guessing, or lying.
q5.explain: Returns depend on things no seller controls, so a guarantee is a false promise.
t3.title: Pyramids and recruiting
t3.define: A **pyramid scheme** pays early members with money from new members. It needs more and more recruits, so it must collapse.
t3.explore: Open the lab. Set {recruits} new members each. Slide the level up and watch the numbers.
q6.prompt: Each member must bring in {recruits} new members. How many people must join at level {level}? Type a number.
q6.hint: Multiply {recruits} by itself {level} times, or read the first box in the lab.
q6.explain: {recruits} multiplied by itself {level} times is {atLvl} people at that level.
q7.prompt: How many people are in the scheme in all, up to level {level}? Type a number.
q7.hint: Read the second box in the lab.
q7.explain: Adding every level up to level {level} gives {everyone} people.
q8.prompt: An offer says: earn money by bringing in your friends. What is true?
q8.opt.a: It cannot go on, because it needs ever more recruits, and most people end up losing
q8.opt.b: Recruiting friends is a normal way to earn income
q8.opt.c: It is safe because friends trust each other
q8.opt.d: It earns more the later you join
q8.fb.b: Earning mainly from recruiting is a red flag. The money comes from new members, not from real value.
q8.hint: Look at how fast the numbers in the lab grow.
q8.explain: The numbers outgrow any town, so the scheme must collapse and the late joiners lose.
t4.title: Red flags
t4.define: Learn the **red flags** of a scam. They are warning signs that something is wrong.
t4.flags: Watch for a guaranteed return, pressure to act now, and secrecy. Also watch for pay for recruiting others, a celebrity "endorsement", and a seller the market **regulator** has not registered.
t4.tradeoff: Even a good investment can lose money. A promise of high returns with no risk is the warning, not the good news.
q9.prompt: A stranger says: only 2 spots left, send money today, and tell no one. Which red flags are these?
q9.opt.a: Pressure to act now, and secrecy
q9.hint: Which words push you to hurry, and which ask you to hide it?
q9.explain: Rushing you and asking you to keep it secret are classic red flags.
q10.prompt: A coin everyone is talking about has doubled in a week. What is the best description?
q10.opt.a: Speculation: a bet on price moves with little real value behind it, not a safe investment
q10.opt.b: A safe investment, because it is rising
q10.fb.b: A fast rise does not make something safe. Betting on price moves is speculation, and it can fall just as fast.
q10.hint: Is there real value behind the price, or only hype?
q10.explain: Betting on hype is speculation. It is not always a scam, but it is not a safe investment either.
glossary.red_flag.def: A warning sign that an offer may be a scam.
glossary.pyramid_scheme.def: A scheme that pays old members with new members' money.
glossary.regulator.def: An official body that sets rules and registers sellers.
glossary.speculation.def: Betting on price moves with little real value behind it.
